codeReview.summary: Thorough, well-executed replacement of all 35 `any` type usages across 13 source files (9 implementation + 4 test). Implementation files use appropriate type narrowing patterns: `ValidationResult[]` for typed arrays, `keyof ValidationResult` for dynamic property access with null guards, `unknown` with safe casting for validation functions, proper React `ErrorInfo` import, and literal union types for enum-like values. Test files use full typed mock objects, `satisfies Partial<AppSettings>` for partial mocking, and `ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>` for mock function typing. One documented eslint-disable exception remains for a mock in layout-navigation.test.tsx. Both `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm test` pass cleanly.

issues.description: Sort comparison operators `<` and `>` are used on values typed as ValidationResult[keyof ValidationResult], which includes string[], boolean, and null. The null guard handles null, but comparing arrays or booleans with `<` would produce incorrect results at runtime. In practice, sorting is only invoked on string/number fields, so this is a theoretical concern. The same pattern exists in results-table-logic.ts. A more precise approach would use a type-safe key constraint or explicit type narrowing.

`validateResult(data: unknown)` does `const record = data as Record<string, unknown>` without checking if `data` is a non-null object first. If `null` is passed, accessing `record.email` would throw TypeError at runtime. This is the same behavior as the original `data: any` code (not a regression), but a guard like `if (!data || typeof data !== 'object')` would make the validation function truly robust against any input.

summary: PASS. The reduce-any-types feature successfully replaces all 35 `any` usages with proper types across implementation and test files. Two commits (a578efb for implementation files, bc76df4 for test files) cover 13 files total. The changes are well-targeted, use appropriate TypeScript patterns (type narrowing, keyof indexing, satisfies assertions, literal unions), and maintain full type safety. Two non-blocking issues noted: (1) sort comparison operators in results-table files work on the full union of ValidationResult property types but are only used with sortable primitives in practice, and (2) data-validation's validateResult doesn't guard against null input (pre-existing behavior). Verification confirms zero `any` type annotations remain in implementation code, and only one documented exception exists in test code. TypeScript compilation and all tests pass.
